adds.title: Guernsey Prison - Wikipedia
adds.summary: Wikipedia article on Guernsey Prison (Les Nicolles), the island's only prison: opened 1989, 11 wings, capacity 139, operated by the States of Guernsey and accommodating male, female and vulnerable prisoners of juvenile and adult ages (population ~99 in November 2024). Contains no birth-sex-vs-identity housing rule, no trans special unit, and no solitary/segregation practice for trans prisoners; verdict thin: no usable finding on the prison-housing axis.

records.note: no prison-housing data found. The mandated enwiki full-text search for 'transgender prisoner Guernsey' (MediaWiki API) returned only generic hits (Transgender rights in the UK, LGBTQ rights by country or territory, For Women Scotland Ltd v The Scottish Ministers) with no Guernsey-specific trans-prisoner placement/segregation content. The one candidate fetch (Wikipedia 'Guernsey Prison', HTTP 200) confirms Les Nicolles is the sole prison - a single mixed-use facility without any documented trans placement rule, special unit, or segregation practice for trans prisoners; Guernsey's ~2011-2018 equality milestones (base-lane sources) cover sexual orientation/marriage, and no documented case or ruling on trans-prisoner housing was located within the fetch budget.

adds.title: Isle of Man Prison - Wikipedia
adds.summary: Wikipedia article on Isle of Man Prison (Jurby), the island's only functioning prison (GBP 41.7m facility at the former RAF Jurby, fully operational 14 August 2008), operated by the Isle of Man Prison Service. Documents separate units for remand and convicted prisoners, female prisoners, young offenders and vulnerable prisoners, plus a segregation unit - but no birth-sex-vs-identity placement rule, no trans special unit, and no trans-specific solitary/segregation practice; verdict thin: no usable finding on the prison-housing axis.

records.note: no prison-housing data found. The mandated enwiki full-text search for 'transgender prisoner Isle of Man' (MediaWiki API) returned only generic hits (Transgender rights in the UK, For Women Scotland Ltd v The Scottish Ministers, LGBTQ rights in the UK) with no Isle-of-Man-specific trans-prisoner placement/segregation content. The one candidate fetch (Wikipedia 'Isle of Man Prison', HTTP 200) confirms Jurby is the single mixed-use facility, with general female/vulnerable-prisoner units and a segregation unit but no documented trans placement rule or special unit; the island's LGR (2009) and equality protections (base-lane sources) say nothing about prison placement, and no documented case or ruling on trans-prisoner housing was located within the fetch budget.
